question: A **uniform** bar magnet of magnetic moment $M$ and moment of inertia $I$ (about a **vertical axis passing through its center and perpendicular to its length**) is suspended so that it performs **small angular oscillations in a horizontal plane** in a uniform magnetic field $B$. Its time period is $T$. If the magnet is cut into two equal parts by a plane **perpendicular to its length** (i.e., each piece has half the length), what will be the new time period $T'$ of **one** piece oscillating about the same type of axis in the same field?
